name: blast-charge-sequence-visual
description: Visual verification of charge loading UI and detonation sequence: explosive selection, amount, stemming, tubing, auto/manual sequencing, and delay patterns. #554: charging now queues a charge_hole PendingAction (a blaster loads one hole at a time, on foot) instead of writing chargesByHole instantly, so a Charge All order is followed by a wait_until proving the landed count only advances as the blaster works through the queue, with a mid-loading screenshot of the ordered/loaded mix.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, a blaster with a bare blasting licence (no vehicle — #554's charge_hole actions are on-foot, requiredVehicleRole: null), plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — #553's automatic drill dispatch needs both to ever land an ordered hole.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:3 spacing:4 depth:6 start:15,15
steps.description: The grid tool's spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts); one increment click on the strip's spacing stepper (data-field="spacing") raises it to 4 before dragging, so the (15,15)-(23,19) rectangle (8x4) computes the declared 3 cols x 2 rows instead of the default-spacing 4x2 (issue #479 follow-up, Finding #4). #553: confirming the grid queues 6 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 6 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm.

expect.note: 2 rows x 3 cols = 6 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 6 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 125).

expect.note: All 6 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

steps.description: Speed up the charge-loading wait below — real-clock auto-tick at 1x would take a long time to drain even a single blaster's queue.

expect.note: #554: Charge All only orders the 6 charge_hole actions — chargesByHole stays empty until the blaster actually loads each hole

steps.description: #554: this click queues one charge_hole PendingAction per hole (requiredSkill: 'blasting', requiredVehicleRole: null — on foot, unlike drilling's drill_rig gate). None of the 6 lands the instant the button is clicked; the wait_until steps right after this one drive the blaster through the queue.

#554/#590: the single staffed blaster claims the nearest ordered hole and loads it, one at a time. Screenshot taken here on purpose, halfway through the batch: 3 holes show the loaded charge visuals while the other 3 (still in plannedChargesByHole) render the lightweight ORDERED ghost marker (CHARGE_ORDERED_COLOR/CHARGE_ORDERED_OPACITY, BlastPlanOverlay.ts) — proving the two are visually distinct. maxTicks/timeoutMs widened to the implementer's own calibrated per-order wait budget (#554 landed). (#554 follow-up: NOT run at 8x speed -- this step deliberately checkpoints a specific mid-load count for a screenshot; speed-8x would overshoot past it before the 200ms poll catches the exact value. The already-generous timeoutMs covers real-time draining at normal 1x speed instead.)

expect.note: half the Charge All order has landed; the other half is still ordered-but-unloaded

steps.description: #554/#590: drain the rest of the Charge All order. Budget doubled off the implementer's single-order figure to cover the remaining sequential loads.

expect.note: Charge All has now landed on every hole

steps.description: Restore normal speed before the remaining player-driven steps.

Per-hole charging is a real control now (gap G3, ChargeHoleList.ts): the Charge step renders a "Per Hole" section, one row per hole keyed by data-hole, each with its own commit button at [data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="charge-hole"]. That button dispatches `charge hole:<id> explosive:<selected> amount:<amount>kg stemming:<stemming>m` from the panel's current product card / amount / stemming values (ChargeStep.chargeHole, Charge.ts) — the same three values Charge All reads, so the steppers have to be driven to the declared numbers first. The explicit [data-step="2"] click is required: Charge All above completed the plan, so the still-armed autoAdvance had already moved the panel to Sequence. 3 amount increments (5 -> 8kg) and 5 stemming increments (2.0 -> 3.0m) reach the declared values. Amount steps by 1kg (data-field="amount", clamped to the selected product's [minChargeKg, maxChargeKg]); stemming steps by 0.2m with a 0.5m floor (data-field="stemming", Charge.ts adjustStemming). Both are plain instance fields on ChargeStep with no reset path, so they carry over from the previous charge step in the same page session — asserted before each commit rather than assumed. #554: this queues a fresh charge_hole order for H1 — chargesByHole['H1'] keeps its already-landed (5kg/2m) value until the new order lands, so chargedCount is unaffected by this click, exactly as it was pre-#554 (Charge All had already charged all 6, and this proves one row overrides one hole without disturbing the count either way).

expect.note: count is unchanged — Charge All had already loaded all 6; this proves one row can re-order one hole, and that the re-order doesn't land instantly either (#554)

steps.description: The [data-step="3"] click is new and load-bearing: the per-hole charge step above disarms autoAdvance by clicking a tab, so the panel no longer walks itself to Sequence. delay_step:25 is the panel's own DEFAULT_DELAY_STEP_MS, so no delay-step stepper click is needed. Sequencing reads state.drillHoles directly and is unaffected by #554 — it does not care whether a hole's charge has landed yet.

Per-hole delay is a relative +/- stepper ([data-hole="<id>"] [data-action="delay-inc"/"delay-dec"], Sequence.ts), stepping by the panel's current delay-step value and clamping at 0. Reaching an exact target is therefore arithmetic on the delay Auto Sequence actually assigned, read out of a real command-mode trace (screenshots/scenario-<name>-command/step-NN-sequence.json's sequenceDelays) rather than computed by re-deriving autoVPattern. Auto Sequence left H1 at 25ms with a 25ms step (traced: step-04-sequence.json), so a single decrement lands exactly on the declared 0.
H2 is Auto Sequence's row-1 lead hole, left at 0ms (traced: step-04-sequence.json), so 2 increments at the 25ms step reach the declared 50.
